headline: China's AI chips set to capture 90% of domestic market as US export controls bite
summary: Cambricon and Huawei are poised to dominate China's AI accelerator market, pushing out Nvidia and AMD as Beijing mandates domestic hardware adoption.
details: China's domestic AI accelerator market is undergoing a seismic shift, with local manufacturers expected to seize nearly 90% of sales by 2026. This dramatic change is driven by U.S. export controls and Beijing's push for self-sufficiency in critical technologies, effectively sidelining major foreign players like Nvidia and AMD.

Nvidia, which held a dominant 66% market share in China's AI accelerator sector in 2024, saw its share plummet to an estimated 40% in 2025 and is projected to fall to just 8% in 2026. CEO Jensen Huang even stated Nvidia's market share in the PRC was 'zero' in the first half of the year, though unofficial channels may still supply some GPUs.

In 2025, China's total available market for AI accelerators reached over 4 million units. While Nvidia still led with 55% market share, shipping 2.2 million units, its closest competitor was Huawei with 812,000 units (20.3%). Other domestic players like Alibaba's T-Head, AMD, Cambricon, and Kunlunxin shipped significantly fewer units.

The Chinese government's active encouragement of domestic AI chip adoption is a key factor. This policy support is expected to significantly boost high-potential domestic players, enabling them to expand their share in the high-end AI server market. The maturing domestic ecosystem in areas like advanced foundry nodes and packaging further strengthens this trend.

Analysts now project Chinese-developed high-end AI processors to see an increase of over 83% year-over-year in 2026. This revised outlook marks a substantial increase from earlier predictions, indicating a faster-than-expected transition towards domestic solutions.

China aims to implement a 'dual-track strategy,' combining AI accelerators from merchant suppliers like Huawei and Cambricon with custom AI ASICs developed by tech giants such as Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance, and Tencent. This approach seeks to reduce reliance on foreign GPUs and build a robust domestic AI infrastructure.

Hyperscale cloud service providers are increasingly opting for their own custom silicon due to cost-effectiveness and optimization for specific workloads. Meanwhile, merchant hardware developers are expected to ramp up production to meet surging demand, further solidifying the shift away from foreign suppliers.
